name: Trichoglossus moluccanus
plant_note: Feeds on nectar and pollen from grevilleas, bottlebrushes, gums and banksias, and on fruit.
habitat: Flowering trees and shrubs, with tree hollows for nesting.
description: A noisy parrot with a blue head, green back and orange chest that travels in fast, screeching flocks. It was introduced to Perth, where it competes with native parrots for hollows.

name: Manorina melanocephala
plant_note: Feeds on nectar from grevilleas, bottlebrushes and gums, and on insects.
habitat: Open woodland and suburbs with lawn and scattered trees. Dense, prickly shrubs give smaller birds shelter from it.
description: A loud grey honeyeater with a black crown and yellow skin behind the eye. Its colonies chase smaller birds out of gardens with few dense shrubs.

name: Gymnorhina tibicen
habitat: Open grassland and lawns with tall trees for nesting.
hazard_note: Some magpies swoop people near their nest in spring. Please keep away from the nest, wear a hat, and walk rather than run past.
description: A black-and-white songbird with a rich, warbling call that hunts for grubs and beetles on lawns.

name: Dacelo novaeguineae
habitat: Woodland and leafy suburbs with large trees and hollows for nesting.
description: A large kingfisher with a famous laughing call that hunts lizards, snakes, insects and worms. It was introduced to south-western Western Australia and Tasmania.

name: Cacatua galerita
plant_note: Eats seeds, nuts, fruit and bulbs, and chews timber and soft wood.
habitat: Woodland and parks with large hollow-bearing trees.
description: A large white cockatoo with a yellow crest and a harsh screech, often seen in noisy flocks.

name: Eolophus roseicapilla
plant_note: Eats grass seeds, grain and roots.
habitat: Open country, parks and lawns with trees for roosting.
description: A pink-and-grey cockatoo that feeds in flocks on the ground.

name: Grallina cyanoleuca
habitat: Open ground near water or wet lawns, with mud for its bowl-shaped nest.
description: A small black-and-white bird that feeds on insects and snails on the ground and calls in duets.

name: Rhipidura leucophrys
habitat: Open ground and lawns with a few shrubs and low branches.
description: A small black-and-white flycatcher that wags its tail from side to side as it chases insects.

name: Malurus cyaneus
plant_note: Shelters in dense, low shrubs and grasses and feeds on small insects among them.
habitat: Thick, low shrubs and tussocks close to open ground. It is one of the first birds to leave a garden without dense cover.
description: A tiny wren with a cocked tail. Breeding males are bright blue and black, and females and young are brown.

name: Acanthorhynchus tenuirostris
plant_note: Feeds on nectar from tubular flowers such as correas, grevilleas and salvias.
habitat: Dense shrubs with tubular flowers through the year.
description: A small honeyeater with a long, fine, curved bill that hovers at flowers.

name: Phylidonyris novaehollandiae
plant_note: Feeds on nectar from grevilleas, banksias and bottlebrushes, and on insects.
habitat: Dense flowering shrubs, especially banksias and grevilleas.
description: A busy black-and-white honeyeater with yellow wing patches and a white eye.

name: Zosterops lateralis
plant_note: Eats insects such as aphids, nectar, and soft fruit, including grapes and berries.
habitat: Shrubs and trees with dense foliage.
description: A small olive-green bird with a white ring around the eye that moves in small flocks.

name: Ocyphaps lophotes
plant_note: Eats seeds of grasses and weeds on the ground.
habitat: Open ground and lawns near shrubs and trees.
description: A grey pigeon with a thin black crest whose wings whistle when it takes off.

name: Threskiornis molucca
habitat: Wetlands, lawns and parks.
description: A large white wading bird with a bare black head and long curved bill that probes lawns for grubs.

name: Vanellus miles
habitat: Short grass and open ground, where it nests in a scrape.
hazard_note: Lapwings swoop people who come near their nest on the ground. Please keep away from the nest until the chicks can fly.
description: A ground-dwelling plover with a yellow face mask and a loud, rattling alarm call.

name: Platycercus elegans
habitat: Forest and leafy gardens with tree hollows for nesting.
description: A crimson parrot with blue cheeks, wings and tail.

name: Strepera graculina
plant_note: Eats fruit and berries, including those of weeds such as privet, and the eggs and chicks of small birds.
habitat: Woodland and suburbs with tall trees.
description: A large black bird with white tail tips and a yellow eye whose ringing call carries far.

name: Anthochaera carunculata
plant_note: Feeds on nectar from grevilleas, banksias, gums and bottlebrushes.
habitat: Flowering trees and shrubs.
description: A large, noisy honeyeater with red wattles on its cheeks and a yellow belly patch.

name: Alectura lathami
plant_note: Rakes leaf litter for insects, seeds and fallen fruit, and builds large mounds of it.
habitat: Rainforest and leafy suburbs with deep leaf litter.
description: A large black bird with a bare red head. Males build mounds of leaf litter up to a metre high to incubate eggs, often in garden beds. It is protected.

name: Acridotheres tristis
habitat: Towns, shopping strips and lawns.
description: A brown bird with a black head and yellow eye skin and legs. It was introduced from Asia and competes with native birds for nest hollows.

name: Passer domesticus
habitat: Towns and farms, close to buildings.
description: A small brown and grey bird introduced from Europe. Males have a grey crown and black bib.
